div.head: I Cn 21
div.ab: And ealle Cristene men we lærað swiðe georne, þæt hig inweardre heortan æfre God lufian ⁊ rihtne Cristendom geornlice healdan ⁊ godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran ⁊ Godes lara ⁊ laga smeagan [⁊ spyrian] oft ⁊ gelome, him sylfum to þearfe.

⁊ ealle Cristene men we lǽrað swiðe georne, þæt hí inweardre heortan æfre God lufian ⁊ rihtne Cristendóm geornlice healdan ⁊ godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran ⁊ Godes lara ⁊ laga smeagan ⁊ spyrian oft ⁊ gelóme, heom sylfum to ðearfe.

And ealle Cristene men we larað swiðe georne, þæt hig inweardlice heortan afre Godd lufian ⁊ rihtne Cristendom geornlice healdan ⁊ godcundan lærewan geornlice hyran ⁊ Godes lára ⁊ laga smeagan ⁊ spyrian oft ⁊ gelome, hym sylfum to þearfe.

Omnes Christianos sedulo commonemus, ut puro corde semper Deum diligant et catholice Christianitatis fidei digne seruiant, sanctis ęcclesię doctoribus deuote pareant, Dei leges et doctrinam subtiliter inuestigent sepius (semper) et assidue, sibimet ad utilitatem.

Docemus etiam omnes Christianos, ut intimo corde semper Deum diligant et rectam Christianitatem diligenter teneant et diuinis doctoribus sollicite obediant Deique doctrinam et legem satagant scire et inuestigent sepe et frequenter, sibimet ipsis ad utilitatem.

⁊ ealle Cristene men we lǽrað swiðe georne, þæt hí inweardre heortan æfre God lufian ⁊ rihtne Cristendóm geornlice healdan ⁊ godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran ⁊ Godes lara ⁊ laga smeagan ⁊ spyrian oft ⁊ gelóme, heom sylfum to ðearfe.

And ealle Cristene men we lærað swiðe georne þæt hig inweardre heortan æfre God lufian and rihtne Cristendom geornlice healdan and godcundan lareowan geornlice hyran, and Godes lara and laga smeagan oft and gelome him sylfum to þearfe.

Und alle Christenmenschen unterweisen wir höchst ernstlich, dass sie stets aus innerstem Herzen Gott lieben und echtes Christenthum willig halten und geistlichen Lehrern eifrig gehorchen und Gottes Lehren und Gesetze oft und emsig bedenken und erforschen, sich selbst zum Nutzen.

And we very earnestly instruct all Christian people always to love God from their inmost hearts and eagerly hold true Christianity and eagerly obey their spiritual teachers, and often and diligently consider and study God's teachings and laws, for their own benefit.

And very zealously we enjoin upon all Christian men that ever, from their inmost hearts, they love God and zealously uphold the true Christian faith, and eagerly obey their spiritual teachers, and frequently and often ponder over and inquire into the precepts and laws of God for their own advantage.

And we most sincerely instruct all Christians to always love God with their innermost hearts and fervently uphold the true Christian faith and readily heed their spiritual teachers, and often and frequently reflect upon God’s precepts and laws for their own benefit.

div.note: In G, ‘⁊ spyrian’ was added in the 16th century in the margin (also in the Wulfstan homily 307). Liebermann compares VIII Atr 43.1; VI Atr 42.2.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 303, October 2026 (MS Cons)
smeagan: B and A add and spyrian, which has been added here in a sixteenth-century hand
